newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel slams Lebanese commander comments.
newsitem.headline: Israel slams Lebanese commander comments.

text.p: Israel said on Tuesday that a Lebanese army chief's comments were part of a "war of nerves" that was slowing down the Middle East peace process.

Lebanese army commander General Emile Lahoud inspected frontline units facing Israeli troops in south Lebanon on Tuesday and ordered them to defend Lebanese territory by all possible means against Israel.

David Bar-Illan, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's communications director, described the comments as "rhetoric... which is all part of the war of nerves which retards rather than advances the peace process."
"We hope both the Lebanese and the Syrians will tone down their rhetoric and sit down at the negotiating table and discuss all issues without preconditions," Bar-Illan told Reuters.
A Lebanese army communique said Lahoud inspected positions of the army's sixth brigade and commando units confronting the Israelis at the south of Lebanon's eastern Bekaa valley.
The troops face Israeli units at the eastern end of a 15-km (nine miles) wide occupied buffer zone intended to prevent cross-border guerrilla raids into Israel.

"He (Lahoud) gave orders to the soldiers emphasising that since Syrian-Israeli (peace) talks stopped the Israeli enemy is trying its utmost to separate the Lebanese and Syrian tracks and is resorting to threats," the communique said.
"The army's duty is to protect its land and counter the enemy with all available means," it added.
Lebanon has reinforced its frontline in the Bekaa valley in the past few days with hundreds of commandos backed by artillery and armoured vehicles.

The reinforcement followed a redeployment of some of Syria's 35,000 soldiers in Lebanon in what was described as a defensive measure after apparent threats of military action in Lebanon by Israeli leaders.
No peace talks have been held between Israel and Syria since Netanyahu, who rejects trading occupied land for peace, won Israel's May elections. Syria demands the return of the Golan.
